domain_rationale: Correctness is decided by host forensics practice: reading syslog auth logs without a year across rotation, utmp/wtmp/btmp login records, an NTP clock step, OpenSSH key fingerprints, TTY-to-session attribution of sudo, and ctime-versus-mtime file timelines to attribute an SSH intrusion. The deliverable is an incident report a response team files, not software behaviour for its own sake.
evidence: instruction.md: 'this triage in forensics'; the report fields are incident-response findings (initial access, attacker sources and accounts, privilege escalation, persistence, first/last activity)
environment/app/docs/case-guide.md: numbered case-handling rules over auth logs, wtmp/btmp, histories, dpkg state and a ctime/mtime listing

planned verifier: reports from hidden generated evidence sets compared field by field (sets order-free) with expectations sealed from solution/model.py, which derives them from the generated scenario, not from the evidence
task.toml: category Security, subcategory Forensics, tags digital-forensics, incident-response
